title: The Ninety-Year Soup
description: It's Founders' Day on Snazzie FM, and the town's perpetual pot of soup has simmered ninety years without ever once going cold. Then the new health inspector calls in to mention the broth was never replaced, the 1934 base is still down there, and the pot has started keeping its own temperature.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and happy Founders' Day. Tonight we honor the pride of this town, the perpetual pot. Ninety years simmering, never once turned off. Mildred, you've stirred that pot your whole life. Welcome.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ninety years. <p:0.3> Same soup. That's the part I keep getting stuck on.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Oh, it's an honor, Ronnie. My mother stirred that pot. Her mother stirred that pot. <p:0.3> You don't turn off a Founder.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And listen to that, Barry. That soft little bubble coming down the phone line. <p:0.3> That right there is the heartbeat of the town.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's a nice bubble. I'll give it that. <p:0.3> Mildred, quick question. When was the last time it was, you know, cold?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Cold? <p:0.3> Why on earth would we let it go cold? Every family adds a little. We've never stopped. We just keep adding.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now that's heritage. Everybody contributing to one big beautiful pot.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: And I add the carrots, Ronnie. <p:0.3> Every Sunday, fresh carrots, peeled myself. So whatever anyone says, the carrots are clean.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Nobody said anything yet, Patricia.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Hi, yes, hello. I'm Darnell, I'm the new health inspector for the county. <p:0.3> So, for the record, I love a tradition. I do. <p:0.3> But I pulled the file on this pot today.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A man who does his homework. Welcome aboard, Darnell.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Thank you. So, for the record, in ninety years, nobody has ever actually replaced the broth. <p:0.3> The 1934 base layer is still in there. At the bottom.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: The original broth. From 1934. Is at the bottom. Right now.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Well of course it is, dear. That's the foundation. <p:0.3> My mother stirred that layer. You don't throw out a Founder.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: See, Darnell, that's not a problem. That's ninety years of love, all the way down.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Right. So, for the record, I asked the gas company who has the burner permit. <p:0.3> They had no record. Because the burner was unplugged. In 1991.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Huh. <p:0.3> Mildred, did the pot just get louder? On its own?

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Wait. <p:0.3> Hold on. If the burner's been off since 1991... <p:0.3> then what's keeping it warm?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: I add the carrots! <p:0.3> The carrots are not the warm part! Talk to someone else!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: It keeps itself warm, dear. It learned. <p:0.3> Around the eighties it just sort of... took over its own temperature. We stopped having to do it.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It LEARNED?! Soup does not learn, Mildred!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A self-warming heirloom. <p:0.3> You can't teach that, Barry. That's heritage.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: So, for the record, I'd like someone to read me the 1934 ingredient list. <p:0.3> Because the first three lines are normal, and then line four is just the word us.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Line four is WHAT?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Don't read line four on the air, dear.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Ma'am, I have to inspect it. I'm coming down to the pot personally tonight.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Carrots!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Founder!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Unplugged!

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Why is it getting warmer while we TALK?!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Folks, the pot is rolling now. A real boil. <p:0.3> Nobody touched it.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: It can hear you, Ronnie. <p:0.3> It does not like the word inspect.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Darnell, do NOT go down to that pot tonight!

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: So, for the record, I'm already in the basement. <p:0.3> And it's... it's looking at me.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, the real question was never whether we should eat it. <p:0.3> It's whether it's gonna let us STOP. <p:0.3> So I'll ask one last time. When was the last time it was cold?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Hear that, Barry? <p:0.5> One slow bubble. Almost like it answered you.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That was a yes. <p:0.3> Ronnie, that bubble was a yes.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Never, Barry. It's never once been cold. <p:0.3> That's heritage. We'll be right back, and Darnell, if you can still hear us down there... hang tight. <p:0.3> Soup's on.
